property_summary: If an address is approved via setApprovedLogger, approvedToLog returns true for that address.
approvedToLog(caller) returns the same boolean as the public mapping approvedLoggers[caller].
If an unapproved caller tries to log Created, the call returns false (i.e., events only emit when caller is approved).

For every caller address the reference contract returns the stored approval mapping value from approvedToLog(caller); the mutant that always returns false violates this because there exist callers for which the stored mapping is true but the mutant still returns false.

For every address x, approvedToLog(x) returns the stored mapping value approvedLoggers[x]; the mutant that always returns false violates this by returning false for some x where approvedLoggers[x] == true.

For any address a, approvedToLog(a) returns the stored mapping value approvedLoggers[a]; the mutant that always returns false will for some fuzzed address a produce approvedToLog(a)==false while the mapping entry approvedLoggers[a] is true (violating the equality).

For every address a, calling approvedToLog(a) returns the stored mapping value approvedLoggers[a]; the mutant that always returns false will for some fuzzed address a make approvedToLog(a) return false while the reference would return true after setting that mapping entry, so the property is violated by the mutant.

For any address a, if the contract's public mapping approvedLoggers[a] is true then calling approvedToLog(a) returns true; the mutant that always returns false will cause approvedToLog(a) to return false for some a even though approvedLoggers[a] is true.

For any caller address X and queried address Y, C.approvedToLog(Y) returns approvedLoggers[Y] (i.e., it uses the provided _caller), whereas the mutant incorrectly returns approvedLoggers[msg.sender], so when msg.sender != _caller the return differs.

For every addresses callerQueried and actualCaller, the reference returns approvedLoggers[callerQueried] (it uses the provided argument) while the mutant incorrectly returns approvedLoggers[msg.sender], so there exists inputs where callerQueried != actualCaller and approvedLoggers differ causing differing return values.

For any queried address X, approvedToLog(X) must return the mapping value approvedLoggers[X] (i.e., it must read the supplied argument, not msg.sender); the mutant that reads approvedLoggers[msg.sender] will return a different result when msg.sender != X and the mapping differs for those two addresses.

For any addresses a (queried) and caller (msg.sender), C.approvedToLog(a) returns approvedLoggers[a]; the mutant returns approvedLoggers[msg.sender], so when msg.sender != a and the mapping differs the mutant's return differs.

For any address x and any caller msg.sender, C.approvedToLog(x) must return the stored mapping value approvedLoggers[x] (it must use the provided argument); the mutant that ignores x and returns approvedLoggers[msg.sender] will differ whenever caller != x and the two mapping entries differ.

For every address input, the reference contract returns approvedLoggers[addr] (so only mapping controls approval); the mutant additionally rejects address(0) and thus for some input (addr == address(0)) its return differs from the reference.

For every address x, the reference returns approvedLoggers[x] (even for address(0)), whereas the mutant additionally forces false for address(0); thus the property: c.approvedToLog(x) == c.approvedLoggers(x) for all x — the mutant violates this when x == address(0).
For every address a, approvedToLog(a) must equal the stored mapping approvedLoggers[a]; the mutant returns false for address(0) even when approvedLoggers[address(0)] is true, violating this rule.

For every address a, approvedToLog(a) must always return the stored mapping value approvedLoggers(a); the mutant erroneously forces approvedToLog(address(0)) to false even when approvedLoggers(address(0)) is true, violating this rule for some input.

For every address a, calling approvedToLog(a) returns the mapping approvedLoggers[a]; the mutant incorrectly forces approvedToLog(address(0)) to false even when approvedLoggers[address(0)] is true, so the universal rule is violated for some input.
Only the contract owner can change approvedLoggers, so after a non-owner attempts to set approvedLoggers to true the mapping must remain false for that address.

Only the contract owner (not an arbitrary caller) can set approvedLoggers; i.e., calling setApprovedLogger by this contract's externally-owned caller should succeed only when that caller is the owner.

For any logger address L and boolean status S, calling setApprovedLogger(L, S) by the owner stores approvedLoggers[L] == S; the mutant inverts the stored value so for some (L,S) the stored value differs.

For any address A and boolean S, when the contract owner calls setApprovedLogger(A,S), the mapping approvedLoggers[A] equals S afterwards (reference); the mutant inverts and will make approvedLoggers[A] == !S for some inputs, so the property detects that difference.

For any owner O, logger L, and boolean S, after O calls setApprovedLogger(L,S), the mapping approvedLoggers[L] equals S; the mutant that stores !_status will violate this for some (L,S) when called by the owner.

For any owner caller and any (logger, status) inputs, when the contract owner calls setApprovedLogger(logger, status) the mapping approvedLoggers(logger) equals status afterwards; the mutant inverts the stored boolean and thus breaks this rule for some inputs.

For any addresses ownerCaller and loggerAddr and any bool status, if the contract owner calls setApprovedLogger(loggerAddr, status) then approvedLoggers(loggerAddr) equals status afterwards; the mutant that stores !_status will cause at least one such call to produce the opposite stored value, violating this rule.

For any caller addr and any _logger address and _status, calling setApprovedLogger(_logger,_status) sets approvedLoggers[_logger] == _status (reference); the mutant that uses msg.sender instead may instead set approvedLoggers[msg.sender], violating this property for inputs where msg.sender != _logger.

For any caller and any target logger address and status, calling setApprovedLogger(target, status) sets approvedLoggers[target] to status in the reference; the mutant that uses msg.sender as key instead will fail this rule whenever caller != target (so there exist fuzzed inputs where approvedLoggers[target] differs).
